newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Hansol Group shares fall on probe report.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Hansol Group shares fall on probe report.

text.p: Shares in six of seven listed firms of the Hansol Group dropped at Wednesday's opening on reports that South Korean prosecutors are probing the group in connection with a scandal involving the president's son.
The Hansol Group, the 16th largest conglomerate, on Wednesday issued a statement denying talk of an influx of funds into the group and saying there had been a misunderstanding.

The Chosun Ilbo newspaper reported that state prosecutors had evidence that the group managed a seven billion won fund on behalf of an associate of President Kim Young-sam's second son, Kim Hyun-chul.
Hansol Paper, the group's flagship company, fell 1,600 won to 19,700.
Hansol Telecom and Electron lost 2,100 won and 1,500 won to 49,800 and 22,800 respectively.
Among other falling Hansol companies, Hansol CSN shed 700 won to 29,600, Hansol Merchant Banking 250 to 8,950 and Hansol Chemical 1,500 to 23,300.
But Hansol Paperboard Co remained unchanged at 6,000 won.

"The report gave a heavy blow to the Hansol shares," said Chang Keun-woo of Daishin Securities. "But the negative impact is not likely to live long as prosecutors' investigation will not badly damage business activities in the group."
